historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (5.7%) tempered to 5% blended over the first five forecast years; equity CAGR is inflated by retained earnings on a low payout and is not a revenue proxy here
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3-yr CAGR +8.8% vs EPS 3-yr CAGR -11.9% and revenue 3-yr CAGR +2.9%: divergence far exceeds 30%. Book value compounds because ZTE retains ~65% of earnings, while earnings themselves fell 40% from the FY2023 peak as the revenue mix shifted to low-margin computing hardware. Do not read the equity CAGR as a growth rate.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - interest income, applied across FY2017-FY2025: 108, -15,039, 112, 2,333, 8,023, -228, 9,606, 3,070, -4,320 (RMB m). CAGRs are undefined on a series with negative endpoints, so 3-yr and 5-yr averages are reported instead. The FY2025 owner FCF of -RMB4.3bn (reported FCF RMB26m less RMB4.35bn interest income) is the H1 FY2026 story in full: working capital absorbed roughly RMB6.5bn as inventories and receivables built for the computing ramp. Interest income has grown from 1.5bn (FY2021) to 4.3bn (FY2025) as the deposit book grew to RMB80bn -- an increasing share of reported FCF is treasury income, not operations, which is exactly why it is stripped.

scenario_narratives.base: The computing pivot works as a volume story but not as a margin story. Government/Corporate (servers, storage, switches to Chinese internet companies and state agencies) keeps growing 30-50% a year off a 35% revenue mix while Carriers' Network shrinks ~10% a year as China's 5G build matures; consolidated revenue grows 8% in FY2026 fading to 2.5%. Consolidated EBITDA margin troughs at ~6.3% in FY2026 and climbs only to 9% by FY2032 -- never back to FY2024's 11.7% -- because computing hardware earns an 11% gross margin against the carrier business's 48%, and Huawei's Ascend ecosystem sets the price. Working capital stays heavy (16% of revenue) because internet-giant customers pay slowly and the hardware is inventory-intensive, so owner FCF margins only reach ~4%. Government grants and VAT refunds (~2% of revenue) continue. No new US export-control action against ZTE itself; chip restrictions constrain product performance but not sales. Terminal value is bound by the 12x cap, not Gordon.
scenario_narratives.bull: 'Connectivity + computing' delivers both legs. Domestic-substitution policy and the East-to-West Computing programme push intelligent-computing revenue up 50%+ for two more years, overseas carrier and terminal business grows in 'large-nation' markets, and consolidated revenue compounds 12/10/8%. Scale in servers, a rising software/platform share (GoldenDB, Nebula models, Co-Sight agent) and the in-house DPU/switch silicon lift the computing gross margin off 11%, so the consolidated EBITDA margin recovers to 11% by FY2031 -- essentially FY2024's level on a larger base. Payment terms improve as ZTE becomes a must-have supplier (wc_capture -12%). The 5G-A/6G cycle gives Carriers' Network a floor from FY2028. Even here the terminal multiple is capped at 12x: a Chinese telecom-equipment vendor excluded from Western 5G markets does not re-rate to a global tech multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: The computing contracts are the 'double-edged sword' analysts have called them. Carrier capex keeps falling, the domestic AI-server market turns into a price war with Huawei, Inspur and H3C, and memory/component inflation squeezes a business reselling hardware at an 11% gross margin; consolidated EBITDA margin settles at 5.5%, below H1 FY2026's 6.5%. Revenue stalls (+3%, 0%, -2%) as internet-company AI capex pauses in 2027-28 after the initial buildout. Working capital intensity rises (-20% capture) as stretched receivables and inventory for low-margin contracts absorb cash -- the FY2025/H1 FY2026 pattern of negative operating cash flow persists. A renewed US action (chip-access tightening or a fresh Entity-List step, given the 2016-2018 history and the 10-year probation period) is not modelled as a shutdown but as the reason margins never recover and government support becomes the profit line. Terminal growth 2%. Net cash of RMB13bn plus the associate stakes keep equity value well above zero even here.

valuation_philosophy.summary: ZTE is valued as a cyclical ICT-hardware manufacturer in transition, on a strict owner-FCF basis: interest income on the RMB80bn deposit book is stripped from the flows and the deposits are credited in the bridge; leases are an operating cost; the convertible is debt. The forward margin is built from components anchored to H1 FY2026, not carried from the FY2024 peak, and working capital is charged on growth because the balance sheet shows growth consuming cash. The scenarios differ on the two axes that matter -- whether the computing mix ever earns a margin, and whether carrier decline plus a possible AI-capex pause stall revenue -- with the bear weighted at 30%. The 12x terminal cap reflects a name that has never re-rated and will not while it is shut out of Western networks.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin path: every 1pt of terminal EBITDA margin is roughly RMB2.4bn of year-10 EBITDA; the base assumes a recovery to 9% that management has not guided to
Working-capital capture: at -16% on growth, a faster ramp of low-margin computing hardware DESTROYS near-term cash; a stall in growth paradoxically releases it
US export controls: a new restriction on ZTE's access to AI accelerators or a fresh Entity-List action would hit the computing segment that provides all of the growth
Customer concentration: top customer ~20%, top five ~45% of revenue, all Chinese state-linked carriers and internet companies whose capex is policy-driven
Government grants and VAT refunds (~2.2% of revenue) sit inside EBITDA; a policy change removes a third of FY2025 EBIT
Net-cash definition: RMB60bn of the RMB81bn cash figure is wealth-management products and bank CDs; the bridge assumes they are recoverable at par
Convertible bond: if the H-share re-rated above HK$29.72 the 132m conversion shares would dilute 2.8% (offset by RMB3.4bn less debt)
FX: a 1% move in CNY/HKD moves the HKD intrinsic value 1%; the rate is at a 52-week high (1.0822-1.1723)

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR consolidated statement of changes in equity (line 12845): share-based payment reserve unchanged at RMB1,116.8m, no charge in FY2025; H1 FY2026 interim (line 9624) likewise unchanged. The 2017/2020 share option schemes were reversed in FY2023 (RMB -290m) and no new scheme has been granted. SBC-zero filer.
inputs.fx_note: CNY -> HKD 1.1721 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-10T03:38Z). Cross-check: USDHKD 7.8472 / USDCNY 6.6922 = 1.1726, and HKDCNY=X 0.8513 = 1/1.1747; all within 0.2%. Per-share values are computed in RMB and multiplied by 1.1721 to give the HKD figures compared with the H-share price. Dual-listing check: the A-share (000063.SZ) closed RMB29.03 on 2026-10-09 = HK$34.03 at this rate, a 64% A/H premium against the H-share HK$20.76; ZTE's A/H premium has persisted for a decade, so the A-share is not a parity check on the rate, only on the direction (an inverted rate would put the A-share BELOW the H-share, which never happens).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T08:08:06Z HKEX regular close (Friday); valuation date is the Saturday after, no after-hours print
inputs.share_count_basis: 4,783.535m ordinary shares (A + H) in issue at 30 June 2026, basic. Held FLAT: SBC is zero and no buyback. The RMB3,584m zero-coupon H-share convertible due Aug-2030 (132.04m potential shares at HK$29.72 strike) is 43% out of the money against HK$20.76 and is carried as DEBT (RMB3,430m liability component inside bonds payable); if-converted would add 2.8% to the count and remove RMB3.4bn of debt -- at the base IV below the strike it does not convert, so the debt treatment is the right one and also the more conservative.
inputs.net_cash_note: Broad net-cash definition, required by the matching-asset rule because RMB4,346m (FY2025) of interest income is stripped from the flows. At 30 June 2026 (interim BS, RMB m): currency cash 24,647.4 less restricted cash 3,304.6 = 21,342.8; trading financial assets at FVTPL (bank wealth-management / structured deposits, rolled ~RMB100bn/yr through investing cash flows) 25,860.9 (the 111.8 of listed equity instruments goes to the bridge instead); debt investments due within one year 14,056.0 and non-current debt investments 19,879.7 (both large-denomination bank certificates of deposit, note V.9/V.21). Total interest-bearing assets 81,139.4. Debt ex-leases: short-term loans 3,847.4 + long-term loans due within one year 10,291.8 + other non-current liabilities due within one year 700.0 + long-term loans 42,719.3 + bonds payable 10,213.7 (incl. convertible 3,430 and MTNs) = 67,772.2. Lease liabilities (633.6 current + 1,002.4 non-current) are excluded under lease treatment (B). Net debt = -13,367.2 (net cash). The naive CSV figure (currency cash only vs total debt) shows RMB43.8bn net DEBT -- that definition is wrong for this balance sheet because it ignores RMB60bn of deposits that fund the interest income being stripped.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows: China 10y CGB ~1.8% (Oct 2026) + 6.0% equity risk premium x beta 1.2 = 9.0% cost of equity; with a net-cash balance sheet WACC = cost of equity, so 9.0%. No ad-hoc premium for export-control/geopolitical risk or the computing-pivot execution risk: those are charged ONCE, in the flows, via the bear path and a 30% bear weight. Same WACC in all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. FY2025 lease cash: RMB578.1m principal (other cash paid in financing, AR line 8217) + ~RMB40m lease interest = ~RMB620m = 0.45% of revenue, charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path. D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 D&A 4,757.8 less ROU depreciation 515.4 = 4,242.4 = 3.17% of revenue). Lease liabilities (RMB1,636m) excluded from net debt. Charged once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated; non-controlling interests RMB215.6m (FY2025 BS; NCI share of profit was -RMB53m FY2025, +RMB32m H1 FY2026) deducted once in the equity bridge. Immaterial either way.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing: non-US cyclical operating company, read owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). ZTE is an ICT equipment manufacturer with project revenue, inventory and receivables -- a cash-flow business, not a bank/REIT/holdco. Statements under PRC ASBEs in RMB; H-share quote in HKD. FY0 = FY2025 (31 Dec); year 1 = FY2026, of which H1 is reported (revenue +9.0%, EBITDA margin ~6.5%, OCF -RMB127m). EBITDA definition used for the margin anchor: operating profit excluding net finance income, associate gains, wealth-management investment returns and fair-value gains, but INCLUDING other income (government grants + software VAT refunds, RMB2,887m = 2.2% of revenue in FY2025 -- recurring but policy-dependent, see bear narrative) and factoring losses on receivables (an operating working-capital cost). FY2025: EBIT 5,238 + D&A 4,758 = EBITDA 9,996 (7.5%); FY2024: 9,249 + 4,969 = 14,217 (11.7%); H1 FY2026: 2,687 + 2,362 = 5,048 (6.5%). Cash tax: income tax expense 11.7% of pre-tax profit FY2025 (9.5% FY2024, 11.2% H1 FY2026) -- 15% high-tech enterprise rate less R&D super-deduction; the PRC cash-flow statement does not isolate income tax paid, so the path ramps the effective rate from 12% to the 15% statutory rate. Working capital: net operating working capital (receivables + receivable financing + prepayments + other receivables + inventories + contract assets + other current assets, less bills and trade payables, contract liabilities, employee benefits, taxes, other payables, provisions) was RMB21.8bn = 16.3% of revenue at FY2025 and RMB24.7bn at H1 FY2026; growth consumes cash, so wc_capture is negative (base -16%). Owner FCF history is lumpy (FY2021 8.0bn, FY2022 -0.2bn, FY2023 9.6bn, FY2024 3.1bn, FY2025 -4.3bn; 5-yr average RMB3.2bn) so the build is component-based, not a margin carry-forward. SBC is zero: house and street bases coincide, band_position is null. Buybacks: none (RMB0 in financing activities FY2017-FY2025); the flat count is a fact, not a convention the company pays for. Terminal cap 12x owner FCF: cyclical, chronically low-multiple name (H-share P/E 8-15x over the decade, 7.1x EV/EBITDA today).

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +8% (H1 actual +9.0%, H2 comps softer as carrier capex keeps falling); computing growth of 30-50% on a 35% mix offsets a ~10% carrier-network decline and flat consumer. Decelerates to 2.5% as the computing mix matures and China AI capex normalises.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 6.3% (H1 actual 6.5%, H2 seasonally weaker). Recovers to 9.0% by FY2032 -- below FY2024's 11.7% because the mix is permanently more computing-heavy (11% gross margin vs 48% carrier). 'Profit growth through quality enhancement' is management's stated FY2026 priority; the path assumes partial, slow delivery.
base.wc_rationale: Net operating working capital 16% of revenue at FY2025; each RMB of growth ties up 16 cents. Bull uses -12% (better payment terms as computing scales); bear -20% (internet-giant customers stretch terms, inventory builds).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: the thesis rests on an unproven pivot (management itself says the computing 'commercial closed-loop' is still in cultivation), the largest customer is ~20% of revenue and the top five ~45%, the last five quarters show accelerating margin compression and negative operating cash flow, and ZTE carries a live US export-control tail risk. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right -- sustained AI capex, a margin recovery in a segment Huawei prices, and no new sanctions. Base 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
